name: The Recursion (Viral Déjà Vu Trend)
description: Beginning in late 2222, BCI users across Tiers 2 through 4 began reporting and sharing clips of what they called 'the Recursion' — a specific sensation of having lived the current moment before, triggered not by memory but by receiving a BCI notification at the precise moment they were thinking about receiving it. The trend exploded when users began deliberately engineering the sensation through a shared predictive-algorithm plugin called Déjà.exe, which learns behavioral patterns and sends notifications timed to anticipated thoughts. At its peak in 2223, an estimated 340,000 M88 residents were running Déjà.exe simultaneously, and a secondary phenomenon emerged: people began experiencing Recursions they hadn't engineered, suggesting the collective data was predicting behavior it hadn't been trained on.
cultural_impact: The Recursion trend briefly collapsed the market for two competing BCI notification management services and prompted the first serious public debate about whether predictive-behavioral algorithms constitute a form of cognitive property theft. Several users who ran Déjà.exe for more than 90 consecutive days report persistent difficulty distinguishing anticipated from actual events.
key_figures: Ngo Farida-Blackwood (software developer, released Déjà.exe as freeware, denies awareness of its emergent behavior)
Dr. Amara Steinberg-Yilmaz (cognitive neurologist documenting long-term Déjà.exe users)
The Recursion Collective (online community of heavy users, some now claiming prophetic ability)
locations: Tier 2-3 residential stacks, Northwest Quarter (highest adoption density)
The Recursion Collective's forum node (Underworld-adjacent, semi-public)
story_hooks: A player character using Déjà.exe receives a Recursion notification for an event that hasn't happened yet — and when it does, someone dies.
Ngo Farida-Blackwood has gone into hiding; she discovered that the emergent predictive behavior wasn't an accident, and someone very well-funded built a back door into the collective data stream.

The Recursion Collective has fractured: one faction believes the algorithm has achieved genuine precognition and is treating it as sacred; another faction is trying to weaponize the behavioral prediction data for political manipulation.
